contract: When a provider search throws an exception that escapes BookFinder.search, CoverSearchManager reports it per provider and SocketAuthority emits cover_search_provider_error to the requesting socket alone with {requestId (echoed), provider (the provider string the client requested, not a canonical name), error (the exception message, which no client parses)}. The search then emits cover_search_complete with no cover_search_result. A custom provider's own HTTP failure is caught inside BookFinder.getCustomProviderResults and its adapter, so it produces no provider error and only a complete; a rejected or cancelled request produces none either.
exceptions: force is not applicable: a provider failure has no force or override mode.

The only offline-reachable trigger is a finder-level exception: a non-string title makes BookFinder.search throw before it contacts any provider. A custom provider answering HTTP 500 is swallowed by getCustomProviderResults and emits no provider error, which the failure scenario asserts instead of inventing an HTTP failure event.
The error text is not pinned: the web client only logs data.error, so the scenarios assert a non-empty string, the echoed requestId and the requested provider name.

invariants.contract: A search whose finder call fails for one provider emits exactly one cover_search_provider_error to the requesting socket with {requestId, provider, error}: requestId echoed, provider the requested provider string, error a non-empty string, followed by cover_search_complete with no cover_search_result. The event is not broadcast to another connection of the same user, another user's socket or an unauthenticated socket. The requested provider name is echoed verbatim, including an unknown slug and a regional audible provider. Each failing search emits its own event and complete, and a failure after a successful search reports only its own requestId without repeating or adding a result. A request rejected for invalid parameters or an unauthenticated socket emits cover_search_error and no provider error. A custom provider's HTTP 500 emits no provider error, no result and one complete while the provider rows stay unchanged.
